chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Sa'id ibn Yasar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had intercourse with his slave-girl who would go and come (i.e., was not permanently confined), and he had practiced withdrawal (azl) with her, and there had been no other intercourse with her. What do you say regarding the child? He said, 'I hold that this child should not be sold, O Sa'id.'

He said: And I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he said, 'Do you accuse her (of impurity/unfaithfulness)?' I said, 'As for an apparent accusation, no.' He said, 'Then do your people (family) accuse her?' I said, 'As for something apparent, no.' He said, 'Then how can you manage for the child not to be attached to you (i.e., not be considered your legitimate offspring)?'

key_terms.لُحُوق: Attachment of lineage (child attached to father)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the lineage and status of a child born to a slave-girl through intercourse with withdrawal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *luhuq* (lineage attachment) in the context of a master's concubine, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the child remains attached to the father and is not sold separately, provided there is no clear evidence of unfaithfulness (*khitmah*). Imam al-Rida (AS) further reinforces this by establishing that the default presumption of legitimacy (*asl al-lahuq*) holds unless the family raises a specific, proven accusation, thereby protecting the child's status and inheritance rights within the Shia jurisprudential framework.
